messages:
alice.mcg: Heads-up — after last night's RBAC role rename rollout some SCIM jobs started failing for a handful of orgs. getting 403 from provisioner and KMS decrypt errors in logs.
benji: Ugh. Which service account is hitting KMS?
alice.mcg: scim-provisioner@redwood-svc. Error snippet: `error=KMSDecryptFailed ctx=attrs: service_account_id=svc_scim_42 cause=invalid_ciphertext`
carla: That usually means the envelope key/alias the service account expects rotated but the envelope metadata wasn't rewrapped. Did the RBAC rename touch any key policies?
alice.mcg: Not that I saw in the PR. The only infra change was the role rename + two config map updates in k8s.
benji: Can you paste the SCIM request payload (redacted) and the SAML mapping that determines extId/role claim? I want to check claim->extid translation.
alice.mcg: Payload (redacted): ```{"userName":"jdoe@example.com","externalId":"team-alpha/jdoe","groups":["alpha-admins"]}``` SAML role mapping in idp: `Attribute name: roles -> transform: split(',', first) -> prefix with tenant:` so new RBAC rename changed group slugs from `alpha-admins` -> `alpha:admins` in the UI
carla: aha. So externalId format changed (slash vs colon). Provisioner uses externalId to look up KMS-wrapped key metadata in Dynamo. mismatch -> lookup returns nil -> decrypt fails.
benji: That explains the invalid_ciphertext. The decrypt call was passing an empty key_ref. Which explains 403 since provisioning logic denies if key metadata absent.
sre-oncall: Quick mitigation idea: roll back the role rename in the authz service or add a temporary translation shim in the provisioner to accept both `team-alpha/jdoe` and `team-alpha:jdoe` formats. Rollback is faster.
alice.mcg: Rollback would be easiest, but that touches many services. We can patch provisioner to be forgiving for 24h. I'll open a canary.
carla: Also add a short-term migration job: scan users with extid containing `:` and create mapping copies with `/`. That avoids double-serving.
benji: For audit trail: note that audit logs currently show success for role rename but no provisioning entries for affected users. We should attach original audit event ids to the migration job so we can replay if necessary.
alice.mcg: Creating a runbook entry now: steps to patch provisioner, migration job, and verification queries. Link: https://confluence.internal/redwood/idp-scim-migrate (draft)
idp-bot: Deploy queued: scim-provisioner patch v2026.03.23-canary -> green on staging.
benji: After patch is live can someone run this query to validate a sample: `SELECT user_id FROM provisioning_jobs WHERE status='failed' AND error LIKE '%KMSDecryptFailed%' LIMIT 50;`
alice.mcg: Running now... returns 28 rows. Picking one: user jdoe, org team-alpha.
carla: When you patch, add explicit logging to include incoming extid and normalized extid resolved so we can see which path matched. Minimal PII.
sre-oncall: Also alerting: add a temporary SLO suppression for the provisioning alert to avoid paging for the known failure window. I'll toggle it.
alice.mcg: Patch is live on canary, running migration job for 10 users first. Results: 10/10 migrated, provisioned, and created audit entries.
benji: Great. Plan: 1) Deploy patch to prod, 2) run full migration with idempotency checks, 3) regenerate KMS envelope metadata only where missing, 4) follow up in next engineering-all-hands.
carla: Postmortem notes:- root cause: role rename changed group slug format without a coordinated mapping in provisioner- contributing: lack of schema-contract test between authz and scim services- remediation: add contract test + pre-commit hook to detect extid format changes + migration tooling
alice.mcg: Filing follow-up ticket for contract test and adding a KMS metadata sanity-check at provisioning start. Ticket: ENGSEC-1729
benji: Marking this thread resolved once prod migration completes. Great work everyone :thumbsup:
